questions.q: Using the method 'Population Density in Cities', work with: area = 100, population = 48000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of density.
Take the relation taught for 'Population Density in Cities' and work with: area = 500, population = 1200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of density.
Explain in your own words what 'Population Density in Cities' refers to.
questions.a: Cities crowd many people onto small land: population density - persons per square kilometre - runs far higher in cities like Gurugram than in villages such as Asadpur Khera in Haryana, and this density drives both the energy and the strains of urban life.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Population Density in Cities'.
questions.a: People per square kilometre is the yardstick of crowding - and cities pack thousands.

concepts.title: Why Cities Grow: Centres of Work and Hope

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Why Cities Grow: Centres of Work and Hope' refers to.
questions.a: Cities attract people because they concentrate jobs, factories, offices, schools, hospitals and markets - offering something for everybody, as the chapter's epigraph puts it - so migration from villages keeps feeding urban growth.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Why Cities Grow: Centres of Work and Hope'.
questions.a: Jobs and services pull migrants in: cities grow because opportunity concentrates there.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Why Cities Grow: Centres of Work and Hope' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Urbanisation: The Process and Its Challenges

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Urbanisation: The Process and Its Challenges' refers to.
questions.a: Urbanisation is the rising share of people living in urban places; as India urbanises, cities strain under slums, housing shortages, traffic, pollution and unequal services, needing planned infrastructure and governance to stay liveable.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Urbanisation: The Process and Its Challenges'.
questions.a: Urbanisation is inevitable - planning decides whether cities become engines or slums.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Urbanisation: The Process and Its Challenges' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'The World's Most Populous Cities' refers to.
questions.a: Giant cities now span the globe - Tokyo, Delhi, Shanghai and other metropolises hold tens of millions, with New Delhi among the world's most populous cities and Seoul in South Korea another megacity - showing that urbanisation is a worldwide phenomenon.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The World's Most Populous Cities'.
questions.a: Megacities of tens of millions now anchor the world economy - and its congestion.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The World's Most Populous Cities' taught, and from which source text?
